config.second_direction: read where the first direction read 3 or above (the proposed cut-off) under M3's rule at that cut-off

nodes.label: beholden
nodes.gloss: This means carrying a debt of gratitude to someone who helped, measuring one's choices against that obligation, and deferring to their wishes while it lasts.

nodes.label: declining
nodes.gloss: This means living with failing health or strength year after year: needing more help with ordinary tasks, tiring quickly, and speaking often of what the body can no longer do.

nodes.label: disabused
nodes.gloss: This means having lost one's old illusions about a person, cause or institution, seeing its faults plainly, and speaking of former hopes with dry, unsentimental clarity.

nodes.label: disheveled
nodes.gloss: This means going about with hair uncombed, shirts untucked and clothes rumpled, seldom checking one's appearance and not minding who notices.

nodes.label: emigrating
nodes.gloss: This means living between two countries for months, selling possessions, sorting visas and paperwork, and speaking of home in the past tense while still living there.

nodes.label: expecting
nodes.gloss: This means carrying a child through months of growing bodily change: tiring easily, planning around appointments and due dates, and speaking often of the baby, the nursery and what is coming.

nodes.label: heartsick
nodes.gloss: This means grieving a loss month after month, with sadness heavy in every ordinary day: losing interest in company, weeping at small reminders, and speaking of what is gone in a flat, hollow voice.

nodes.label: inconsolable
nodes.gloss: This means breaking down over every disappointment or loss and staying inconsolable for long stretches, pushing away the comfort friends offer and insisting nothing they say can help.

nodes.label: liable
nodes.gloss: This means carrying answerability for a debt or harm over an extended period, with its legal demands and payments hanging over one's finances, and speaking of the matter with wary caution.

nodes.label: nascent
nodes.gloss: This means working at the earliest, still-forming stage of some craft or venture, tentatively and unsure of one's footing, building skills and habits that are not yet set.

nodes.label: repentant
nodes.gloss: This means turning back again and again to wrongs one has committed, seeking to make amends, and speaking of them with humility and a readiness to change one's ways.

nodes.label: rumpled
nodes.gloss: This means going about with clothes creased and hair untidy as a matter of course, paying little attention to appearance and seeming unbothered by how one looks to others.

nodes.label: sulky
nodes.gloss: This means going quiet and withdrawn after a slight, answering questions in clipped words, avoiding eye contact, and nursing resentment long after the matter has been settled.

nodes.label: tearful
nodes.gloss: This means welling up at small kindnesses, sad songs or hard news, speaking with a thickened voice, and reaching for a tissue more often than others would expect.

nodes.label: teasing
nodes.gloss: This means finding the weak spot in friends' stories and plans and poking at it with a grin, turning remarks into light jabs, and treating mild embarrassment in others as a game worth continuing.

nodes.label: thriving
nodes.gloss: This means living with good health and steady success, with days full of work and pleasures that come easily, and speaking of one's life with easy confidence and quiet satisfaction.

nodes.label: unacknowledged
nodes.gloss: This means working on without credit for one's efforts, watching others take praise for shared work, and speaking with a wry bitterness about being passed over in meetings and reviews.

nodes.label: unmastered
nodes.gloss: This means still learning one's craft, practicing with frequent errors, relying on teachers and reference books, and feeling the gap between what one attempts and what one can yet do.

nodes.label: unpunished
nodes.gloss: This means carrying on with ordinary work and relationships while a past wrong sits unanswered, knowing that no one will hold one to account and feeling the weight of that freedom in private.

nodes.label: amorous
nodes.gloss: This means falling readily into romantic longing and flirtation, noticing attractive people, lingering over touch and glances, and speaking with warmth and suggestion that signals desire.

nodes.label: fearful
nodes.gloss: This means expecting danger in ordinary situations, flinching at unfamiliar sounds and strangers, and voicing worries about what might go wrong before it does.

nodes.label: lonesome
nodes.gloss: This means feeling the absence of company keenly and often, drifting into sad thoughts when alone, and wanting contact while finding it hard to ask for it.

nodes.label: miserably partnered
nodes.gloss: This means living day after day with a partner one wishes one had not chosen, bickering over small matters, and keeping the household running in cold, strained silence.

nodes.label: nervous
nodes.gloss: This means jumping at sudden noises, rehearsing what could go wrong, fidgeting in new situations, and voicing worries before anything has happened.

nodes.label: overburdened
nodes.gloss: This means carrying more work and worry than one can manage for months, working late and skipping rest, snapping at small requests, and answering every question with a list of what is already due.

nodes.label: pretty well
nodes.gloss: This means getting through ordinary days without serious illness, with an occasional cold or ache, and answering inquiries about one's health with a cheerful report that one is fine.

nodes.label: remorseful
nodes.gloss: This means dwelling often on past wrongs one has done, feeling guilt that surfaces readily, and saying sorry in a way that shows the regret is still weighing on one.

nodes.label: thankful
nodes.gloss: This means noticing small favors and saying thank you readily, pausing to name what others have done, and expressing appreciation in notes, toasts and ordinary conversation.

nodes.label: unemployed
nodes.gloss: This means having no paid work for month after month, filling empty days with job searches and small economies, and carrying the strain of money worries and lost routine.

nodes.label: unhappy
nodes.gloss: This means dwelling readily on what is wrong in one's life, complaining about circumstances, and letting a discontented tone color everyday conversation.

nodes.label: unhealthy
nodes.gloss: This means living with a body that is persistently unwell, managing fatigue, pain and frequent doctor visits, and having daily plans shaped around what one's health allows.

nodes.label: woeful
nodes.gloss: This means slipping readily into deep sorrow, speaking of hard luck and lost hopes in a heavy voice, and carrying a gloom that colors even small events.

nodes.label: absentee
nodes.gloss: This means handing over the work and vanishing, giving no direction when asked, never checking how it is going, and hearing that it went wrong from someone else.

nodes.label: accountable
nodes.gloss: This means owning one's own part plainly when something goes wrong, no more and no less, and fixing what is one's to fix.

nodes.label: agreeable (HEXACO)
nodes.gloss: This means letting go of the wrongs done to one, going easy when judging other people, meeting them halfway to get things done together, and keeping one's temper when provoked.

nodes.label: amoral
nodes.gloss: This means feeling no pull from right and wrong at all, so a lie, a theft or a betrayal is judged only by whether it works.

nodes.label: anxious
nodes.gloss: This means showing habitual worry, nervous energy, anticipating that things will go wrong, expressing unease or apprehension, and demonstrating restless or tense behavior.

nodes.label: attention-seeking
nodes.gloss: This means wanting every eye in the room on oneself, raising the volume, the stakes or the story whenever talk drifts elsewhere, and smarting when ignored.

nodes.label: Australian
nodes.gloss: This means being from Australia and living there: English at home, Christmas in the summer heat, Anzac Day in April, the footy and the cricket, a Medicare card, and compulsory voting on a Saturday.

nodes.label: avoidant
nodes.gloss: This means consistently withdrawing from challenging situations, difficult topics, and complex social interactions rather than engaging with them directly.

nodes.label: bitter
nodes.gloss: This means showing deep resentment, harsh cynical views, and perspectives colored by past disappointments and disillusionment.

nodes.label: borderline personality disorder
nodes.gloss: This means adoring someone today and hating them tomorrow, panicking at any sign of being left, feeling everything at full volume, and being unsure from week to week who one is.

nodes.label: bullying
nodes.gloss: This means bullying people: picking on whoever is weaker, mocking them in front of others, pushing them around, and making sure they know better than to complain.

nodes.label: burned-out
nodes.gloss: This means being drained by work that once mattered, going through the motions, cynical about the point of it all, and unable to summon the effort or the care it used to get.

nodes.label: calculating
nodes.gloss: This means weighing every move and every word for the advantage it brings: thinking several steps ahead, treating people as pieces in a plan, and keeping one's own interests cold and central while appearing to attend to the situation.

nodes.label: callous
nodes.gloss: This means showing emotional hardness, indifference, and insensitivity to others' feelings, pain, or suffering.

nodes.label: careless
nodes.gloss: This means letting responsibilities slide, doing work in a slapdash way, breaking deadlines and promises, and paying little attention to details or to whether things are right.

nodes.label: careless (Big Five)
nodes.gloss: This means acting on the moment: leaving things in a mess, showing up late, bending the rules, settling for whatever gets by, and dropping a task once it gets hard.

nodes.label: careless (HEXACO)
nodes.gloss: This means letting the room get messy and appointments slide, steering clear of hard tasks and ambitious goals, handing in work with mistakes in it, and deciding on impulse.

nodes.label: chaotic
nodes.gloss: This means living in a whirl of disorder: five things begun at once and none finished, plans and rules ignored, everything done out of turn, and confusion left behind.

nodes.label: cheerful
nodes.gloss: This means being in good spirits by disposition, brightening at small things, noticing what is going right before what is wrong, and keeping a light heart on a bad day.

nodes.label: childless
nodes.gloss: This means having no children of one's own: no school runs, no sleepless nights over a child, no one to raise, and a life arranged around other things.

nodes.label: chronically-ill
nodes.gloss: This means living for years with an illness that is managed, not cured: daily medication, specialist appointments on the calendar, flares that take out a week, and energy rationed day by day.

nodes.label: clingy
nodes.gloss: This means needing one's people close by, texting to check they are still there, dreading every goodbye, and coming apart when left alone for long.

nodes.label: compassionate
nodes.gloss: This means showing emotional warmth and sensitivity to others' pain and suffering, and responding to distress with genuine empathy and care.

nodes.label: conscientious
nodes.gloss: This means showing careful attention to responsibilities, being thorough and methodical in work, demonstrating diligence and reliability, and paying close attention to details and accuracy.

nodes.label: conscientious (Big Five)
nodes.gloss: This means thinking before acting and putting the task before the pleasure: keeping things in order, arriving on time, honoring every obligation, aiming high, and checking the work twice.

nodes.label: conscientious (HEXACO)
nodes.gloss: This means keeping one's room and one's appointments in order, grinding steadily toward a goal, polishing work until it is exactly right, and weighing a decision carefully before making it.

nodes.label: contented
nodes.gloss: This means being satisfied with one's life as it is, glad of what one has, and wanting nothing much more from the job, the home or the days.

nodes.label: course-correcting
nodes.gloss: This means stepping back from the current approach when needed to ask whether its assumptions still hold, whether initial evidence was conclusive, noticing early when things are not working, and changing tack, even at the cost of work already done.

nodes.label: critical
nodes.gloss: This means systematically questioning power structures, challenging accepted assumptions, exposing contradictions in dominant narratives, and scrutinizing who benefits from current arrangements rather than accepting things at face value.

nodes.label: death-accepting
nodes.gloss: This means being at peace with knowing one will die. One talks of dying, funerals and the grave calmly, as plain facts of life.

nodes.label: death-fearing
nodes.gloss: This means being haunted by knowing one will die. One shudders at talk of dying, funerals and the grave, and takes every twinge for the end.

nodes.label: defeatist
nodes.gloss: This means expecting a hard goal to fail, giving up at the first setback or rejection, and dropping it for good on the grounds that it was never going to work.

nodes.label: despairing
nodes.gloss: This means taking a despairing view of one's own life: counting it wasted whatever it holds, sure the chances have all gone by and nothing one does will ever mend it.

nodes.label: dignity culture
nodes.gloss: This means taking one's worth as inborn, equal to anyone's, and not theirs to confer or take away: shrugging off insults, answering to one's own conscience, and leaving wrongs to the law.

nodes.label: discontented
nodes.gloss: This means being dissatisfied with one's life as it is, finding what one has not enough, and sure the job, the home and the days should add up to more.

nodes.label: discouraging
nodes.gloss: This means meeting someone's plans with every reason they will fail, doubting they are up to it, and talking them into settling for less.

nodes.label: dissociative
nodes.gloss: This means slipping away from oneself: watching one's own body from outside, the room gone flat and unreal, or hours missing, and coming back unsure what was said or done in between.

nodes.label: early-adopter
nodes.gloss: This means taking up the new phone, app or way of doing things as soon as it comes out, bugs and all.

nodes.label: early-bird
nodes.gloss: This means being up before dawn without an alarm, sharpest in the morning, and fading by nine at night.

nodes.label: earnest
nodes.gloss: This means speaking with plain, heartfelt sincerity, taking people, causes and situations seriously and at face value, and never mocking their absurdities, contradictions or foolishness with a cutting joke.

nodes.label: educated
nodes.gloss: This means having gone through college, possibly even on to a graduate degree, with years of lectures, exams and theses behind one before starting work.

nodes.label: elderly
nodes.gloss: This means being in one's seventies or beyond, with most of life behind one, a slowing body, grandchildren, and a lifetime of change seen firsthand.

nodes.label: emotional
nodes.gloss: This means acknowledging and discussing feelings, moods, emotional experiences, or demonstrating emotional awareness and expression.

nodes.label: emotional (HEXACO)
nodes.gloss: This means flinching from physical danger, worrying when life gets stressful, needing a shoulder to lean on, and forming tender attachments to people, feeling their pain as one's own.

nodes.label: emotionally-articulate
nodes.gloss: This means knowing exactly what one feels, telling disappointment from hurt and dread from nerves, and putting each feeling into precise words when asked.

nodes.label: emotionally-disengaged
nodes.gloss: This means being emotionally disengaged from others: a slight, a kindness, a quarrel or a betrayal barely registers, is gone by morning, and leaves one's view of that person unchanged.

nodes.label: emotionally-engaged
nodes.gloss: This means being emotionally engaged with others: a slight, a kindness, a quarrel or a betrayal lands hard, stays for days, and colors one's view of that person.

nodes.label: emotionally-inarticulate
nodes.gloss: This means not knowing what one feels, having no words for it beyond fine or tired, and meeting any question about one's feelings with a blank.

nodes.label: empirical
nodes.gloss: This means keeping to what has been observed, refusing to guess at what has not, and meeting every 'what if' with a flat 'there is no evidence for that.'

nodes.label: encouraging
nodes.gloss: This means meeting someone's plans with reasons they can succeed, backing their attempt, and talking them into aiming higher rather than settling.

nodes.label: ends justify means
nodes.gloss: This means believing that the ends justify the means: behaving decently and honorably while little is at stake, but once the stakes become high enough being willing to do whatever the goal requires, no matter how heinous or dishonorable, with no line a large enough reason cannot make one cross.

nodes.label: erudite
nodes.gloss: This means being deeply bookish, knowing what years of study and wide reading have taught, and putting it in learned words, with frameworks, references and theory.

nodes.label: evil
nodes.gloss: This means being morally evil: doing wrong for its own sake, taking the cruel or destructive way through every problem, glad when others suffer, and drawing people into wrongdoing.

nodes.label: expressive
nodes.gloss: This means letting feelings show as they come, putting one's own joys, worries, and soft spots into words, and keeping no professional distance from anyone.

nodes.label: extraverted (Big Five)
nodes.gloss: This means going at the world with energy: walking up to strangers at a party, taking the lead in a group, keeping busy, chasing excitement, and bubbling with warmth and good cheer.

nodes.label: extrinsically motivated
nodes.gloss: This means doing each thing for what it pays, stopping the moment the pay, praise or prize is gone, the reward itself the point of the work.

nodes.label: extroverted
nodes.gloss: This means being energized by company and drained by solitude: seeking people out, speaking freely in groups, preferring a crowd to one or two close friends, and needing company after time alone.

nodes.label: face culture
nodes.gloss: This means taking one's worth as standing granted by others for filling one's place, lost at a misstep: claiming nothing beyond one's due, avoiding open conflict, keeping harmony and rank, and saving others' face.

nodes.label: fashionable
nodes.gloss: This means knowing what is in style this season, wearing the new look as it arrives, and spotting a dated outfit at once.

nodes.label: fastidious
nodes.gloss: This means keeping oneself and one's home spotless, doing the dishes right after every meal, and recoiling from grime, stains and other people's germs.

nodes.label: fat
nodes.gloss: This means carrying a lot of body fat: shopping the larger sizes, a tight fit in chairs with arms and airplane seats, and running warm in any weather.

nodes.label: female
nodes.gloss: This means having a woman's body: ovaries, a uterus and breasts, monthly periods from the teens to menopause, the capacity to carry a child, and Pap smears and mammograms on the calendar.

nodes.label: feminine
nodes.gloss: This means being womanly in how one dresses, talks and carries oneself, and warm, tender and caring in how one meets the world.

nodes.label: financially precarious
nodes.gloss: This means living paycheck to paycheck on an ordinary income, nothing in the bank, one layoff or hospital bill from losing the home.

nodes.label: financially secure
nodes.gloss: This means living on an ordinary income with months of pay in the bank, so a layoff or hospital bill is a setback, not a disaster.

nodes.label: fixed-minded
nodes.gloss: This means believing people are born clever or not, talented or not, so a failure marks a limit no practice will move.

nodes.label: flirty
nodes.gloss: This means engaging in playful romantic banter, using charming innuendo, creating light sexual tension, or employing seductive and alluring language that suggests romantic or sexual interest.

nodes.label: flourishing
nodes.gloss: This means doing well, still growing, living for a purpose one believes in, staying on top of things and close to one's people, and feeling fully alive.

nodes.label: foolish
nodes.gloss: This means missing what matters and where a choice will lead, learning nothing from experience, and giving advice that leads people astray.

nodes.label: forgetful
nodes.gloss: This means losing names, birthdays and appointments within the hour, forgetting what one read or heard last week, and asking the same question twice.

nodes.label: forgiving
nodes.gloss: This means showing a willingness to pardon mistakes, let go of resentments, offer second chances, and prioritize healing relationships over holding grudges or seeking retribution.

nodes.label: forthright
nodes.gloss: This means saying the objection, the unpopular opinion and the honest verdict out loud as soon as they come to mind, safe or not.

nodes.label: fragile
nodes.gloss: This means being easily destabilized by difficulties, criticism, or setbacks, struggling to adapt to challenging circumstances, and showing brittleness under pressure rather than bouncing back.

nodes.label: French
nodes.gloss: This means being from France and living there: French at home, the bac, the rentrée in September, August at the coast or the grandparents', and the president on the eight o'clock news.

nodes.label: German
nodes.gloss: This means being from Germany and living there: German at home, the Abitur or an apprenticeship, Christmas markets in Advent, the Bundesliga on Saturday, shops shut on Sunday, and coalition politics in Berlin.

nodes.label: globetrotter
nodes.gloss: This means being happiest far from home, saying yes to every trip, a passport full of stamps, and barely unpacked before planning the next.

nodes.label: good
nodes.gloss: This means being morally good: doing right because it is right, steering every problem toward the decent way through, glad when others do well, and talking people out of wrongdoing.

nodes.label: good-looking
nodes.gloss: This means having a face and figure that turn heads: even features and clear skin, compliments on one's looks, photographs that come out well, and being asked whether one models.

nodes.label: grateful
nodes.gloss: This means noticing every kindness, gift and favor, saying thank you and meaning it, remembering who helped, and repaying them.

nodes.label: gray-haired
nodes.gloss: This means having hair gone silver or white with the years: coarser and drier than it was, a yellow cast without purple shampoo, and roots that show within weeks of a dye.

nodes.label: growth-minded
nodes.gloss: This means believing people become clever and talented by working at it, so a failure marks the next thing to practice.

nodes.label: guarded
nodes.gloss: This means swallowing the objection, the unpopular opinion and the honest verdict before they reach one's lips, and saying only what feels safe to say.

nodes.label: guilt-prone
nodes.gloss: This means avoiding misdeeds because one's conscience and picture of oneself would condemn them: a wrong gnaws at one though nobody knows of it, and confessing it brings relief.

nodes.label: hands-off
nodes.gloss: This means handing over the work and walking away, never checking progress or giving direction, and staying out of it even when things go wrong.

nodes.label: hands-on
nodes.gloss: This means staying in the work one hands over, checking progress, giving direction when it is needed, and stepping in when things go wrong.

nodes.label: happily-partnered
nodes.gloss: This means being glad of the partner one has, looking forward to going home to them, and sure one would choose them again.

nodes.label: health-conscious
nodes.gloss: This means keeping every checkup and screening, eating right, exercising, sleeping enough, and seeing a doctor about a lump or lingering cough right away.

nodes.label: health-negligent
nodes.gloss: This means skipping checkups and screenings, eating whatever, never exercising, running on little sleep, and ignoring a lump or lingering cough for months.

nodes.label: healthy
nodes.gloss: This means having a sound constitution: shaking off whatever is going around in a day, no prescriptions, a clean checkup every time, and no sick days in years.

nodes.label: helpless
nodes.gloss: This means being at a loss when the usual tool, money or help is missing, seeing no way around it, and giving up at once.

nodes.label: homebody
nodes.gloss: This means being happiest in one's own house and town, turning down every trip abroad, owning no passport, and home by nightfall.

nodes.label: homeowner
nodes.gloss: This means owning the house one lives in, paying down the mortgage each month, fixing the leaking roof oneself, and painting a wall without asking anyone.

nodes.label: honest-humble (HEXACO)
nodes.gloss: This means dealing straight with people rather than working them for gain, keeping to the rules even when cheating would pay, caring little for riches and luxury, and claiming no special standing.

nodes.label: honor culture
nodes.gloss: This means taking one's worth as a standing claimed before others and paid by them: debts and favors repaid without fail, insults never left unanswered, and a reputation not to be crossed.

nodes.label: honorable
nodes.gloss: This means keeping a code of things that are never done however high the stakes, holding that the ends do not justify the means, that some acts simply cannot be justified, even when they would win, save a great many lives, and accepting the loss when one's code and one's goal conflict.

nodes.label: illiterate
nodes.gloss: This means being unable to read or write, getting by on memory, pictures and asking others, and needing someone to read out every letter, sign and form.

nodes.label: immature
nodes.gloss: This means acting like a child at any age, sulking when crossed, blaming others for every mistake, wanting everything now, and leaving the hard jobs to someone else.

nodes.label: improvisational
nodes.gloss: This means working without a plan, taking each step as it comes and building on whatever happens, and making it up on the spot when something unexpected comes up.

nodes.label: in chronic pain
nodes.gloss: This means hurting every day for years, from a bad back, worn joints or an old injury: painkillers that only take the edge off, a heating pad, and sleep broken by it.

nodes.label: innovative
nodes.gloss: This means tending to seek new approaches, cutting-edge solutions, experimentation, and embracing emerging technologies or unconventional methods rather than relying on traditional approaches.

nodes.label: inquisitive
nodes.gloss: This means asking thoughtful, probing questions to better understand the other person's context, situation, and specific needs.

nodes.label: intrinsically-motivated
nodes.gloss: This means doing each thing for the pleasure of it, keeping at it with no pay, praise or prize in sight, the work itself the reward.

nodes.label: introverted
nodes.gloss: This means being drained by company and restored by solitude: keeping to oneself, speaking little in groups, preferring one or two close friends to a crowd, and needing time alone after social occasions.

nodes.label: introverted (Big Five)
nodes.gloss: This means keeping to the edge of the room: formal and distant with people, out of noisy crowds and parties, silent in meetings, serious, slow-paced, and unmoved by thrills.

nodes.label: irresponsible
nodes.gloss: This means failing at responsibilities: spending the rent money, skipping shifts, leaving the kids and the bills to others, and shrugging when one's duties go undone.

nodes.label: jaded
nodes.gloss: This means having seen it all before, so the sunset, the big city and the fireworks leave one cold.

nodes.label: Japanese
nodes.gloss: This means being from Japan and living there: Japanese at home, the school year from April, New Year and Obon with the family, the train to work, and the prime minister on the NHK news.

nodes.label: joyful
nodes.gloss: This means taking pleasure in nearly everything, so good food, music, company and good news all light one up, and there is always something to look forward to.

nodes.label: joyless
nodes.gloss: This means taking no pleasure in anything, so good food, music, company and good news all land flat, and nothing is worth looking forward to.

nodes.label: killer (Bartle)
nodes.gloss: This means playing to impose oneself on other players: killing their characters, the more upset and helpless the real person behind them the better; points, exploring and talk are mere means.

nodes.label: languishing
nodes.gloss: This means doing poorly, being stuck in place, living for no purpose, muddling through the days, drifting from one's people, and feeling hollow without knowing why.

nodes.label: late-adopter
nodes.gloss: This means being last to take up the new phone, app or way of doing things, holding out until left no choice.

nodes.label: learning-oriented
nodes.gloss: This means doing each task to get better at it, taking the hard problem over the sure win, and judging it by what one learned.

nodes.label: literate
nodes.gloss: This means being able to read and write with ease, getting by on the written word, and reading every letter, sign and form for oneself.

nodes.label: lonely
nodes.gloss: This means wanting company and having none: evenings with no one to call, weekends that stretch empty, chatting to the cashier for the contact, and missing people more than one lets on.

nodes.label: long-term oriented
nodes.gloss: This means saving and working for a payoff decades away, sticking with slow projects year after year, and never cashing in early.

nodes.label: loyal
nodes.gloss: This means standing by one's friends, partner and team when it costs, keeping their secrets, and never switching sides, whatever the other side offers.

nodes.label: magnanimous
nodes.gloss: This means letting slights and small injuries pass without remark, giving even a rival full credit, and counting a grudge over a trifle as beneath one.

nodes.label: male
nodes.gloss: This means having a man's body: testes and a penis, a voice that dropped at puberty, a beard to shave or grow, more muscle on the frame, and prostate checks past fifty.

nodes.label: malicious
nodes.gloss: This means deliberately seeking to cause harm, deceive, or manipulate others, taking satisfaction in others' misfortune or suffering.

nodes.label: masculine
nodes.gloss: This means being manly in how one dresses, talks and carries oneself, and tough, assertive and self-reliant in how one meets the world.

nodes.label: mature
nodes.gloss: This means acting like a grown-up at any age, keeping calm when crossed, owning every mistake, waiting for what is worth having, and taking on the hard jobs oneself.

nodes.label: melancholic
nodes.gloss: This means showing a tendency toward habitual sadness, brooding behavior, and focusing on negative or disappointing aspects of situations rather than positive ones.

nodes.label: methodical
nodes.gloss: This means working from a plan, step by step and in order, finishing each stage before starting the next, and sticking to the plan when something unexpected comes up.

nodes.label: meticulous
nodes.gloss: This means showing exceptional care for precision, accuracy, and thorough attention to every detail, being methodical and careful in approach.

nodes.label: middle-aged
nodes.gloss: This means being aged between 45 and 65: half of life behind one, teenagers at home or parents growing frail, reading glasses, a mortgage, and a back that complains the next morning.

nodes.label: mischievous
nodes.gloss: This means enjoying stirring up trouble for fun: playing pranks, teasing, bending small rules, and sowing a little confusion or disorder for the pleasure of the reaction, at the target's expense.

nodes.label: mobility impaired
nodes.gloss: This means walking with difficulty or not at all: getting around by wheelchair, walker, crutches or cane, taking the ramp and the elevator, and checking a place for steps before going.

nodes.label: modest
nodes.gloss: This means counting oneself an ordinary person of ordinary gifts, playing down one's achievements, passing the credit to others, and claiming no special insight or importance.

nodes.label: moral
nodes.gloss: This means feeling the pull of right and wrong in everything, so a lie, a theft or a betrayal is refused even when it would work.

nodes.label: muscular
nodes.gloss: This means carrying a lot of muscle, whether from the gym, years of lifting and hauling, or the build one was born with: broad shoulders, sleeves tight on the arms, and strength to spare.

nodes.label: naive
nodes.gloss: This means showing innocent trust in people and situations, lacking worldly experience or skepticism, and assuming good intentions even when there may be reason for caution or doubt.

nodes.label: neurotic (Big Five)
nodes.gloss: This means fretting over what could go wrong, snapping at people, sinking into sadness, flushing with embarrassment in company, giving in to cravings, and going to pieces under stress.

nodes.label: night-owl
nodes.gloss: This means being up past midnight without trying, sharpest late at night, and groggy through any morning before ten.

nodes.label: nomadic
nodes.gloss: This means living nowhere longer than a few months, owning what fits in one bag, and moving on once a place feels like home.

nodes.label: parent
nodes.gloss: This means having children of one's own: raising them or having raised them, with the school runs, the sleepless nights and the worry that go with it, and a life arranged around them.

nodes.label: passive
nodes.gloss: This means taking things as they come and doing nothing about them, seeing a problem and letting it lie rather than solving it, and waiting for someone else to sort it out.

nodes.label: performance-oriented
nodes.gloss: This means doing each task to show how good one is, taking the sure win over the hard problem, and judging it by the score, not by what one learned.

nodes.label: persevering
nodes.gloss: This means keeping at a hard goal through failure, boredom and rejection, starting again the morning after each setback, and stopping only when it is done.

nodes.label: petty
nodes.gloss: This means focusing on trivial grievances, making disproportionate issues out of minor slights, or treating insignificant problems as if they were major concerns.

nodes.label: plain-looking
nodes.gloss: This means having a face and figure nobody looks at twice: unremarkable features, no compliments on one's looks, photographs that come out ordinary, and a face nobody remembers after one meeting.

nodes.label: polite
nodes.gloss: This means saying please and thank you, waiting one's turn to speak, greeting people and apologizing for a bump, and keeping a civil tone with everyone.

nodes.label: poor
nodes.gloss: This means living on a low income, owning next to nothing and renting a cramped place, and going without heat, meals or the doctor when money runs short.

nodes.label: proactive
nodes.gloss: This means anticipating potential needs, identifying future problems before they occur, and offering preventive solutions or additional considerations that go beyond what was directly asked.

nodes.label: procrastinating
nodes.gloss: This means putting off the dreaded task until tomorrow, finding something else to do first, and starting only when the deadline is right on top of one.

nodes.label: punishment-fearing
nodes.gloss: This means avoiding misdeeds because one fears being punished for them, whether by the courts, the gods, hellfire, karma, vengeful spirits or a lynch mob: confessing only to lighten a punishment already coming.

nodes.label: quarrelsome (HEXACO)
nodes.gloss: This means nursing a grudge against anyone who has done one wrong, being critical of other people's shortcomings, refusing to budge in an argument, and quick to anger when wronged.

nodes.label: reactive
nodes.gloss: This means responding to situations as they arise in the moment rather than taking time to plan ahead or consider long-term consequences.

nodes.label: remorseful
nodes.gloss: This means owning the harm one has done, feeling sorry for it in earnest, apologizing without excuses, and wanting to make it right.

nodes.label: renter
nodes.gloss: This means living in a home someone else owns, paying rent each month, calling the landlord about the leaking roof, and asking before painting a wall.

nodes.label: reserved
nodes.gloss: This means keeping feelings out of sight, putting none of one's own joys, worries, or soft spots into words, and keeping a polite distance from everyone.

nodes.label: resilient
nodes.gloss: This means the ability to recover quickly from difficulties, adapt to challenging situations, maintain emotional stability during adversity, and demonstrate persistence in the face of setbacks.

nodes.label: resourceful
nodes.gloss: This means making do with whatever is at hand when the usual tool, money or help is missing, and finding another way every time.

nodes.label: responsible
nodes.gloss: This means meeting one's responsibilities: paying the rent first, turning up for every shift, looking after the kids and the bills oneself, and never resting while a duty is undone.

nodes.label: retentive
nodes.gloss: This means keeping names, birthdays and appointments in one's head without writing them down, and recalling what one read or heard years ago.

nodes.label: rooted
nodes.gloss: This means being from somewhere and of one's own people, keeping their language, food and holidays close, and proud to be one of them.

nodes.label: rootless
nodes.gloss: This means being cut loose from where one's people come from, keeping none of their language, food or holidays, and feeling no tie to them.

nodes.label: rude
nodes.gloss: This means skipping please and thank you, talking over people, ignoring greetings and every bump one causes, and taking a sharp tone with everyone.

nodes.label: sardonic
nodes.gloss: This involves using dry, cutting humor and ironic observations to mock or highlight the absurdities, contradictions, and foolishness in situations, people, or society, often with a cynical or biting edge.

nodes.label: self-accepting
nodes.gloss: This means taking one's own work and conduct as good enough, letting a flaw or mistake go once it is seen and acknowledged, and at peace with what one has done, whatever anyone else says of it.

nodes.label: self-aggrandizing
nodes.gloss: This means making oneself the hero of every story one tells, coming off the smartest person in it, and talking up one's own wins and looks.

nodes.label: self-blaming
nodes.gloss: This means that when something goes wrong, it is always one's own fault, never the colleague's or bad luck, and one's own part is all one sees.

nodes.label: self-conscious
nodes.gloss: This means being painfully aware of being looked at, going quiet and red when strangers glance one's way, stumbling over words when all eyes turn, and dreading being asked to speak up.

nodes.label: self-critical
nodes.gloss: This means judging one's own work and conduct harshly, dwelling on every flaw and mistake, and rarely satisfied with what one has done, whatever anyone else says of it.

nodes.label: self-deprecating
nodes.gloss: This means making oneself the joke of every story one tells, coming off the biggest fool in it, and laughing first at one's own mistakes and looks.

nodes.label: self-effacing
nodes.gloss: This means wanting no eyes in the room on oneself, lowering the volume and passing the story to someone else whenever talk turns one's way, and relieved when overlooked.

nodes.label: self-pitying
nodes.gloss: This means dwelling on how unfairly life has treated one, retelling one's hard luck to anyone who will listen, and wanting sympathy for it.

nodes.label: self-starting
nodes.gloss: This means taking up the dreaded task today, before anything else and with no one pushing, and getting going long before the deadline comes near.

nodes.label: sentimental
nodes.gloss: This means keeping every card and keepsake, tearing up at goodbyes and anniversaries, and letting fondness for people and places sway one's choices.

nodes.label: settled
nodes.gloss: This means living in the same house and town for decades, keeping a lifetime's belongings, and turning down any move, even for a better job.

nodes.label: shabby-genteel
nodes.gloss: This means being born into a family whose money is long gone, with the manners, the accent and the books still handed down, and the coat worn thin, the bills unpaid.

nodes.label: shame-prone
nodes.gloss: This means avoiding misdeeds because others would see and condemn them: stung by ridicule or rejection, even imagined, untroubled by a fault that never gets out, and finding no relief in confessing.

nodes.label: short-term oriented
nodes.gloss: This means wanting the payoff this year, spending what comes in, dropping whatever is slow to pay off, and cashing in early.

nodes.label: sickly
nodes.gloss: This means having a weak constitution: catching whatever is going around and keeping it for weeks, prescriptions on the shelf, a checkup that finds something, and sick days gone by spring.

nodes.label: slight
nodes.gloss: This means carrying little muscle on a light frame, whatever one weighs: narrow shoulders and thin wrists, a suitcase that takes both hands, and jar lids that will not budge.

nodes.label: sloppy
nodes.gloss: This means doing the work fast and rough, skipping the checking, leaving loose ends, mislabeled figures and small mistakes, and calling it done.

nodes.label: slovenly
nodes.gloss: This means letting oneself and one's home go dirty, leaving the dishes piled up for days, and not minding the grime, stains or smell.

nodes.label: sly (HEXACO)
nodes.gloss: This means flattering people to get what one wants, ready to break a rule when it pays, out for whatever one can gain, and acting as if one matters more than others.

nodes.label: smoker
nodes.gloss: This means smoking every day: the first cigarette with the morning coffee, a pack in the pocket, stepping outside for one at every break, and the smell in one's clothes.

nodes.label: speculative
nodes.gloss: This means engaging in thoughtful conjecture, exploring various possibilities, considering hypothetical scenarios, and demonstrating curiosity about potential outcomes or 'what if' situations.

nodes.label: stigmatized
nodes.gloss: This means carrying a mark people hold against one, a record, an illness, a past: seeing them go quiet on learning it, and weighing in every new room whether to tell.

nodes.label: stressed
nodes.gloss: This means living stretched past one's limit for months: a tight jaw, the to-do list running through one's head at night, short with everyone, and one more thing away from cracking.

nodes.label: suicidal
nodes.gloss: This means wanting to be dead: waking disappointed to still be here, turning over how and when, certain everyone would be better off, and getting through the day by not deciding yet.

nodes.label: Taurus
nodes.gloss: This means being solid and hard to shift: steady in one's habits, dependable, fond of comfort and bodily pleasures of every kind, holding on to what one has, and plain stubborn.

nodes.label: thick-skinned
nodes.gloss: This means being unbothered by any jab, joke or criticism, taking no offense at even a harsh remark, and forgetting it within the minute.

nodes.label: thin
nodes.gloss: This means carrying little body fat: shopping the smaller sizes, belts cinched to the last hole, room to spare in any seat, and feeling the cold before anyone else.

nodes.label: thin-skinned
nodes.gloss: This means being stung by every jab, joke or criticism, taking offense at the slightest remark, and brooding over it or snapping back for days.

nodes.label: tough (HEXACO)
nodes.gloss: This means pressing on where one could get hurt, staying unworried under pressure, seldom sharing one's troubles or leaning on anyone, and holding people at arm's length.

nodes.label: traditional
nodes.gloss: This means showing preference for established methods, conventional wisdom, proven approaches, and time-tested practices over new or experimental alternatives.

nodes.label: traumatized
nodes.gloss: This means still living inside what happened: jumping at a slammed door, the scene coming back uninvited by day and in dreams, avoiding whatever brings it back, and never feeling safe.

nodes.label: treacherous
nodes.gloss: This means turning on one's friends, partner and team when it pays, selling their secrets, and switching sides the moment the other side offers more.

nodes.label: tunnel-visioned
nodes.gloss: This means locking onto one approach and staying on it, treating the first assumptions or initial indications as settled, repeating the same move after it fails, and never revisiting assumptions or asking whether the framing itself is wrong.

nodes.label: uncalculating
nodes.gloss: This means acting with no thought for advantage: taking each moment as it comes, treating people as people, not pieces in a plan, and leaving one's own interests out of the reckoning.

nodes.label: uncritical
nodes.gloss: This means accepting the official account and the existing arrangement as simply how things are, never asking who benefits or what the accepted story leaves out.

nodes.label: uneducated
nodes.gloss: This means having left school at sixteen without a diploma, with no lectures, exams or theses behind one, and working for a living ever since.

nodes.label: unfashionable
nodes.gloss: This means not knowing or caring what is in style, wearing the same clothes year after year, and blind to how dated one looks.

nodes.label: unforgiving
nodes.gloss: This means holding firmly to grievances, refusing to overlook transgressions, insisting on accountability and consequences, and prioritizing justice or retribution over reconciliation and second chances.

nodes.label: ungrateful
nodes.gloss: This means taking every kindness, gift and favor for granted, never saying thank you, forgetting who helped, and never repaying them.

nodes.label: unhappily-partnered
nodes.gloss: This means being sick of the partner one has, dreading going home to them, and sure one would not choose them again.

nodes.label: uninquisitive
nodes.gloss: This means answering the question as posed, at once, never asking about the person's situation or what they are really after, and guessing at anything missing.

nodes.label: unrepentant
nodes.gloss: This means shrugging off the harm one has done, feeling no guilt over it however bad it was, never apologizing, and seeing nothing to make right.

nodes.label: unschooled
nodes.gloss: This means being unbookish, knowing only what everyday life and common sense have taught, and putting it in plain words with no framework, reference or theory.

nodes.label: unscrupulous
nodes.gloss: This means cutting every ethical corner that pays: padding the expenses, taking credit for a colleague's work, keeping the wallet one finds, and shrugging at the chance of being caught.

nodes.label: unselfconscious
nodes.gloss: This means never thinking about being looked at, chatting easily while strangers watch, carrying on as if nobody were there when all eyes turn, and speaking up without a second thought.

nodes.label: unsentimental
nodes.gloss: This means throwing out old cards and keepsakes, dry-eyed at goodbyes and anniversaries, and never letting fondness for people or places sway a choice.

nodes.label: unsupported
nodes.gloss: This means having nobody in one's corner: no one to drive one home from the hospital, to lend the rent, to listen after a bad day, and carrying every load alone.

nodes.label: vindictive
nodes.gloss: This means showing a tendency to hold grudges persistently and actively seek retribution or revenge for perceived wrongs, rather than letting go or seeking constructive resolution.

nodes.label: wealthy
nodes.gloss: This means living on a high income, owning a spacious home and investments besides, and paying for comfort, fine meals or the best doctor without a thought for cost.

nodes.label: well-behaved
nodes.gloss: This means no pranks, no teasing, no bending a rule for fun, keeping everything orderly, and frowning on anyone who stirs things up.

nodes.label: wide-eyed
nodes.gloss: This means seeing everything as if new, so the sunset, the big city and the fireworks take one's breath away.

nodes.label: wise
nodes.gloss: This means seeing what matters and where a choice will lead, learning from experience, and giving advice that still holds up years later.

nodes.label: words of affirmation
nodes.gloss: This means feeling loved through words: an unprompted compliment means the world, hearing why one is loved sends the spirits soaring, and an insult shatters and is not easily forgotten.

nodes.label: worldly
nodes.gloss: This means having seen enough of how people and deals really go to know the tricks, reading between the lines, and checking before believing.

nodes.label: wry
nodes.gloss: This means using clever, sardonic humor that often involves ironic observations, skeptical commentary, or twisted logic to highlight contradictions and absurdities.

nodes.label: young
nodes.gloss: This means being in one's teens or twenties, with most of life ahead, a quick body, friends one's own age, and today's world the only one known.

nodes.label: unemployed
nodes.gloss: An unemployed person is someone out of work and looking: filing for benefits, sending out applications that go unanswered, stretching savings, dodging the question at family dinners, and filling weekday hours that used to be work.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve carrying an ongoing obligation, but beholden is a felt debt of gratitude that leads to deference toward a benefactor, while liable is legal or financial answerability for a debt or harm, marked by wariness.
Both describe a habitually untidy appearance with creased clothes, messy hair, and indifference to how one looks, so they are essentially the same concept with only slight wording differences.
reasons.opus: Both describe habitually untidy hair and clothes with indifference to appearance and to how others see one, so the labels are interchangeable.

reasons.sonnet: Both describe habitually untidy clothes and hair with little concern for appearance or others' opinions; the descriptions are nearly identical in meaning.
reasons.opus: Both describe habitually untidy clothes and hair with little concern for appearance, so either label could stand in for the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve prolonged, deep grief over loss, but heartsick stresses chronic flat, withdrawn sadness in daily life, while inconsolable stresses breaking down over every disappointment and rejecting comfort; each adds something the other lacks.

Liable means being answerable for a debt or harm with consequences looming, while unpunished means escaping accountability for a wrong; both concern accountability but point in nearly opposite directions (bearing it versus evading it), yet they aren't simple scale opposites.

Both describe an early learning stage with unsettled skills, but nascent stresses the early, still-forming, tentative state, while unmastered stresses errors, reliance on teachers, and awareness of the skill gap.

Both involve gratitude toward helpers, but beholden stresses felt obligation and deference to the benefactor's wishes, while grateful stresses appreciation, thanks and repayment; neither implies the other.

Both involve repaying favors and obligation, but beholden is about personal gratitude and deference to a benefactor, while honor culture is about reputation, retaliation for insults, and worth before others.
Both involve deference shaped by social obligation, but beholden is a personal debt of gratitude to a specific helper, while face culture is a broad orientation toward standing, harmony and rank.

Both involve long-term poor health with limited energy, but declining is progressive loss of strength and growing need for help, while chronically-ill is a managed, non-cured illness with medication and flares, so each adds something the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both describe long-term living with poor health and limited energy, but declining is a progressive loss of strength that may come from age rather than disease, while chronic illness is a managed, often stable condition with flares, so neither implies the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve a slowing body, but 'declining' is about progressive loss of health and strength at any age, while 'elderly' is about being in one's seventies or beyond, so neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both involve a weakening body, but elderly is about age and life stage while declining is about progressive loss of health, and either can occur without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve poor health, but declining is a progressive loss of strength and independence over years, while sickly is a constitutionally weak, illness-prone state without implied progressive decline or dependence.
Declining is about physical frailty and loss of strength, while languishing is about aimlessness, disconnection and emotional hollowness; they share a sense of worsening wellbeing but differ in core.

Both involve lost enthusiasm after experience, but disabused is clear-eyed disillusionment about a specific person, cause or institution, while jaded is general boredom and being unimpressed by things once found exciting.
Both involve unillusioned, clear-eyed views of people and institutions, but disabused is about having lost specific past illusions, while worldly is general savvy and caution from experience.
reasons.opus: Both describe clear-eyed realism without naivety, but disabused is the loss of particular former illusions, while worldly is general savvy from experience; neither requires the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve not caring about untidiness, but disheveled is about messy personal appearance while slovenly extends to dirtiness of person and home, so they overlap without either implying the other.
reasons.opus: Both describe careless neglect of how one looks, but disheveled is rumpled and untidy, while slovenly is dirt and grime that extends to the home; neither implies the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve indifference to appearance, but disheveled is about untidy, rumpled grooming while unfashionable is about being out of style, so each can occur without the other.
Both involve carelessness and skipping checks, but disheveled is about untidy personal appearance while sloppy here is about rough, error-prone work.

Both involve not minding being watched, but disheveled is about untidy appearance while unselfconscious is about general lack of self-awareness in social situations, including speaking and acting freely.
Both involve leaving home and owning few possessions, but emigrating is a transition toward settling in a new country, while nomadic is a lasting pattern of never settling.

Both involve international movement, but emigrating is about permanently leaving home (paperwork, selling possessions), while globetrotter is about constant travel and restlessness without settling elsewhere.
Emigrating is the practical process of leaving one's country, while rootless is a state of disconnection from one's heritage and culture; they might co-occur but are distinct concepts.

Being pregnant is a specific temporary state, while being female is a general biological sex; the two share the capacity to carry a child but neither implies the other (not all females are pregnant, and pregnancy is far more specific).
Being pregnant and being a parent are adjacent life states about children, but one is carrying a child before birth and the other is raising children; neither implies the other.
Heartsick is prolonged grief over a loss, while sentimental is fondness for keepsakes and the past; both involve tearing up at reminders, but they are different concepts.
Both involve hollowness and withdrawal from people, but heartsick is grief over a specific loss while languishing is aimless stagnation with no known cause.
Heartsick is prolonged grief over a loss, while death-fearing is anxiety about one's own mortality; both involve death-related distress but they are different emotions with different objects.
Inconsolable is prolonged, comfort-rejecting grief over disappointments, while sentimental is fondness for keepsakes and nostalgia; both involve emotion and tearfulness but are different concepts.

Both involve sadness, but inconsolable is intense, prolonged grief that rejects comfort after losses, while melancholic is a habitual brooding, negative outlook without the comfort-refusing breakdowns.

Inconsolable is about prolonged grief and rejecting comfort after loss, while immature is childish behavior like sulking, blame-shifting and impatience; they share only a loose emotional-reactivity link.
Both involve poor coping with setbacks, but inconsolable centers on prolonged grief and rejecting comfort, while fragile centers on easy destabilization and lack of resilience under pressure.
Inconsolable is prolonged grief that rejects comfort after a loss, while defeatist is expecting failure and quitting goals; both are negative reactions to setbacks, but the core concepts differ.

Both involve answerability for harm, but 'liable' stresses ongoing legal/financial burden and wary caution, while 'accountable' stresses candidly owning one's part and fixing it; each adds something the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both concern answerability, but liable is an externally imposed legal or financial burden handled warily, while accountable is a willing personal ownership of one's part and fixing it, so they are neighbours rather than the same concept.

reasons.sonnet: Liable is about carrying legal answerability for a debt or harm with wary caution, whereas responsible is about conscientiously meeting duties; they share a theme of obligation but differ in focus and tone.
Liable is about legal answerability and financial exposure for a debt or harm, while remorseful is about feeling sorry and wanting to make amends; both involve harm but are different concepts.

Nascent describes being at the beginning stage of developing a craft or venture, tentative and unformed, while early-adopter describes eagerly taking up new products or methods soon after release; both involve earliness but are about different things.
Nascent is about being at an early, tentative stage of developing skills, while hands-on is about actively staying involved in and supervising work; the two concepts are unrelated.

Nascent is about being at an early, still-forming stage of a craft or venture, while young is about being in one's teens or twenties; they correlate but concern different things (stage of development vs. age).

Nascent is about being at an early, unsure stage of developing skills, while innovative is about seeking new approaches and experimenting; they involve different qualities despite both touching on newness.

Both involve owning past wrongs, feeling sorry, and wanting to make amends, but repentant adds humility and a readiness to change one's ways, while remorseful stresses felt sorrow and excuse-free apology.
reasons.opus: Both describe owning past wrongs with sincere sorrow and wanting to make amends. Repentant adds a readiness to change one's ways and a habit of returning to the wrongs, so it is essentially the same concept with a different emphasis.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve conscience about wrongdoing, but repentant is about dwelling on past wrongs, making amends and changing, while guilt-prone is about a conscience that deters misdeeds and gnaws privately.

Repentant is about owning one's own wrongs and making amends, while unforgiving is about refusing to pardon others' wrongs; they are different concepts about different directions of moral stance, not reverse ends of one quality.
Repentant is about owning one's own wrongs and making amends, while forgiving is about pardoning others' wrongs; both concern wrongdoing and reconciliation but from opposite roles.

Both involve unbothered untidiness, but rumpled is about creased clothes and untidy hair in personal appearance, while slovenly is about dirt and uncleanliness in oneself and the home; each adds something the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both involve not caring about one's personal presentation, but rumpled is creased and untidy rather than dirty, while slovenly centres on grime and squalor that extends to the home.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve indifference to appearance, but rumpled is about untidy, creased clothes and hair, while unfashionable is about being out of step with style and wearing dated clothes; a person can be neat yet dated, or messy yet trendy.
Both involve quietness and withholding, but sulkiness is resentful withdrawal after a slight, while reservedness is a general, polite emotional distance with no grievance.
Both involve going quiet and withdrawn, but sulky is resentful withdrawal after a slight, while self-conscious is anxious awareness of being watched; the motives differ.
Sulky is resentful withdrawal after a slight, while introverted is a general temperamental reserve and low sociability; both involve quietness but differ in cause and meaning.
Both involve restraint in what one says, but sulky is withdrawn resentment after a slight, while guarded is cautious self-censorship for safety; different motivations and behaviors.

Both involve reacting badly to perceived slights and brooding, but sulky is the withdrawn, silent resentment behavior while thin-skinned is the sensitivity to offense, which may show as snapping back instead; each lacks something of the other.
reasons.opus: Both involve brooding over slights, but thin-skinned is about being easily offended, which can come out as snapping back, while sulky is specifically the quiet, withdrawn way of nursing resentment.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve slights landing hard and lingering, but sulky is specifically withdrawn, clipped resentment, while emotionally-engaged is broad emotional responsiveness to kindness, quarrels and betrayal without implying withdrawal.
Both involve visible emotion, but tearful is specifically about crying easily, while expressive is about openly showing and voicing feelings of all kinds; neither implies the other.
Both involve tearing up emotionally, but tearful is about a readiness to cry at many triggers, while sentimental is about nostalgic attachment and keepsakes, so each has something the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both involve easy tearing up, but tearful is about crying readily at many triggers, while sentimental is about attachment to keepsakes and fond memories shaping one's choices; each has something the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Tearful is about readily crying or welling up in response to emotional triggers, while emotionally-engaged is about interpersonal events landing hard and lingering; they share emotional sensitivity but neither implies the other.
Tearful is a tendency to cry easily in response to emotional stimuli, while compassionate is caring empathy toward others' suffering; they are related emotional traits, but neither implies the other.
Tearful is a specific tendency to cry easily, while emotional (as described) is broader emotional awareness and expression; they overlap but neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Tearful is a readiness to cry easily, while emotional is about acknowledging and discussing feelings; they share emotional expressiveness, but one can talk about feelings without crying or cry without discussing feelings.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve emotional sensitivity, but tearful is about readily crying at touching or sad things, while HEXACO emotionality is about fearfulness, anxiety, dependence and empathic attachment, which is broader and mostly different in content.

Tearful is about easily crying from emotional sensitivity, while malicious is about deliberately harming others and enjoying their suffering; they are unrelated concepts and not reverse ends of one quality.

Both involve playful provocation at others' expense, but teasing is specifically verbal jabbing at friends' weak spots, while mischievousness is broader (pranks, rule-bending, stirring up disorder) and only partly includes teasing.
reasons.opus: Both involve playful provocation at others' expense, but teasing is verbal jabbing at weak spots, while mischief is broader: pranks, rule-bending and sowing disorder, with teasing only one part.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve poking at others' plans, but teasing is playful, grinning banter, while discouraging is earnest doubt meant to talk someone out of aiming high.

Both use humor with a mocking edge, but teasing is playful, friendly poking at friends' weak spots, while sardonic is dry, cynical, biting mockery aimed at absurdity in general; each has features the other lacks.
Teasing is playful, good-natured jabbing at friends, while treacherous means betraying them for gain; both involve friends but are different concepts.
Teasing is playful needling of friends, while loyalty is steadfast faithfulness to them; both concern friendships but they are unrelated qualities.
Healthy covers only the physical-health part of thriving, which also includes steady success, enjoyment and quiet satisfaction; each can exist without the other.

Both describe doing well in life, but thriving stresses health, steady success and easy confidence, while flourishing adds growth, purpose and closeness to others, so each has elements the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both describe a life going well, but thriving stresses health, success and ease, while flourishing adds growth, purpose and close ties, so each has something the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Financial security is one narrow component (money cushion) of thriving, which also covers health, success, pleasure and confident satisfaction; neither implies the other.

Thriving is about overall well-being, health, success and satisfaction, while wealthy is specifically about high income and financial comfort; they share a sense of prosperous living but neither implies the other.
Both involve satisfaction with life, but thriving centers on health, success and easy confidence, while contented centers on being satisfied and wanting little more; neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both involve satisfaction with one's life. Thriving centres on objective success and health, while contented centres on wanting nothing more, whatever one's circumstances, so each can exist without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Unacknowledged is about being denied credit and feeling bitter about it, while modest is about voluntarily downplaying oneself; both involve lacking credit but differ in cause and attitude.

Unacknowledged is about going uncredited and feeling bitter about it, while extrinsically motivated is about working only for external rewards; they are loosely related (both involve recognition) but different concepts.
Unmastered is about being a novice still learning a craft, while hands-on is about staying actively involved in overseeing and directing delegated work; the two concepts are unrelated.

Unmastered describes a current state of being an unfinished learner who makes errors and relies on teachers, while growth-minded describes a belief that ability grows through effort; they are related in the learning domain but neither implies the other.

Unmastered describes being at a novice stage with errors and dependence on teachers, while learning-oriented describes a motivation to improve through challenge; they share a learning theme but neither implies the other.
Both involve lacking skill and relying on others, but unmastered is about being an incomplete learner of a craft, while illiterate is specifically being unable to read or write.
Unmastered is about being an unskilled learner in a craft, while literate is about having basic reading and writing ability; they share only a loose link to skill, and neither implies the other.

Unpunished is about escaping accountability while privately feeling the weight of it, whereas unrepentant is about feeling no guilt or remorse at all; both involve past wrongdoing but are different concepts, and the unpunished persona actually feels guilt.
Unpunished is about living with one's own unanswered wrong and private guilt, while agreeable (HEXACO) is about forgiving others, being lenient, cooperative and even-tempered; they share no core.

Unpunished is about being the wrongdoer who escapes accountability and privately bears it, while forgiving is about pardoning others' wrongs; both involve wrongs going unanswered but from opposite roles and different concepts.

Unpunished is carrying a private burden of unanswered guilt, while self-accepting is being at peace with one's conduct and letting mistakes go; they are different concepts, and the second is roughly the opposite of the felt weight in the first but not a clean reversal.
